steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Collecting like terms: only terms with identical variables and powers can be combined

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Expanding brackets: multiply each term inside by the term outside (FOIL for double brackets)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Difference of two squares: a^2 - b^2 = (a + b)(a - b)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Perfect square trinomials: a^2 +/- 2ab + b^2 = (a +/- b)^2

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Expand and simplify (3x - 2)(x + 4) - (x - 1)^2 | Factorise completely: 6x^2 + 13x + 6 | Simplify: (x^3 - 8)/(x^2 - 4)

steps.title: Lesson plan
steps.body: Starter (5 min): Recall prior knowledge of algebraic expressions with quick questions. Teaching (15 min): Work through each of the learning objectives, explaining principles step by step. Key points review (5 min): Revisit the key points together, confirming understanding. Worked example (10 min): Model the example question: Simplify fully: (2x^2 + 3x - 2)/(x + 2) - (x^2 - 4)/(x - 2). Solution: Factorise: (2x-1)(x+2)/(x+2) - (x-2)(x+2)/(x-2) = (2x-1) - (x+2) = x - 3 Practice (10 min): Students attempt the practice questions independently; circulate and support. Plenary (5 min): Review answers and address misconceptions.

steps.title: Homework
steps.body: Expand and simplify (3x - 2)(x + 4) - (x - 1)^2 Factorise completely: 6x^2 + 13x + 6 Simplify: (x^3 - 8)/(x^2 - 4) Divide 2x^3 - 5x^2 + 3x - 1 by (x - 2) using polynomial division Given f(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6, show (x-1) is a factor and factorise fully Simplify: (2x^2y⁻^3)^3 ÷ (4x⁻¹y^2)^2
